notes: Handles the internal issuer, site-block precedence, HTTP-only sites, Tailscale names and case-insensitive matching, but it refactors the existing split code and builds one policy per name that depends on consolidation, so its output diverges from the reference and it fails the hidden test despite very thorough tests (including a comparison against the dummy-site-block config).

Per-name policies with an explicit internal issuer, an existing-policy check that includes internalAP, and case-insensitive dedup are reasonable, and the tests are strong (including site-block equivalence), but it always emits base policies and orders them differently from the reference, failing the hidden test, and it refactors existing site-block code beyond what was needed.

Reasonable single-policy approach with lowercasing and internal-issuer handling, but it refactors existing code (dropping the warnings pointer), always creates a base policy whether or not it carries anything, and ignores internalAP subjects; it fails the hidden test, though its table-driven and adapt tests are good.

Mostly works: it handles HTTP-only sites, site-block precedence and the internal issuer, but it always builds a base policy (empty, noisy policies when there are no global options) and ignores internalAP subjects when checking for an existing policy, so it diverges from the expected output and fails the hidden test. It also refactors the existing split logic (dropping the warnings pointer) and adds unrequested lowercasing.

Wires the option in, but a list of only internal names (e.g. `localhost`) never gets the internal issuer at adapt time, it copy-pastes the public/internal split logic, and it alphabetically sorts the subject order; it fails the hidden test.

It only separates internal names when they are mixed with public names, so a list of only internal names (e.g. localhost/IPs) never gets the internal issuer the spec requires; it also sorts subjects, always creates base policies, duplicates the split logic inline, and fails the hidden test despite broad tests.

Matches the reference implementation exactly (internalAP for internal names, a policy only when global defaults exist, site-block policy wins) and adds thorough unit and adapt tests covering repeated options, auto_https off, HTTP-only sites, existing policies and no site blocks.

The production code matches the reference, including append-on-repeat parsing, internal issuer via internalAP, skipping names a site block already has a policy for, no empty policy without global defaults, and the hasGlobalACMEDefaults helper; it adds thorough unit tests and caddyfiletest fixtures covering every listed requirement.
